status_detail: Three-pass production review published 38 exact, previously absent SHA-256 indicators from six direct primary research reports: six malicious Zimbra CVE-2026-73570 stages from Microsoft Threat Intelligence, two NetScaler CVE-2026-88771 post-exploitation payloads from LevelBlue SpiderLabs, ten Warlock ransomware or malicious-DLL artifacts from Symantec Threat Hunter Team, four live CloudSyncD droppers from Jamf Threat Labs, ten 2CLoader samples used to deliver Vidar, Remus, and XWorm from Zscaler ThreatLabz, and six operator-built Platypus C2 agents recovered by TENEX from active NetScaler exploitation infrastructure. Daily-Threat-Intel supplied eleven SHA-256 candidates; eight qualified after direct-source review. Ten current MalwareBazaar records were inspected and rejected because the individual records did not provide a named family plus sufficiently direct malicious-deployment evidence. The review excluded one miner, one hacktool, one inaccessible ThreatFox record, suspicious-only files, an AV/EDR killer, a vulnerable driver, development-only samples, a partial-content hash, MD5-only IOCs, and otherwise valid samples beyond the per-family diversity cap. Six current security-news sources were opened for discovery and campaign context and traced back to original reports; none were treated as sole proof.
